claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by accessing the official eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to gather some information about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, let me ask about your child's age:**

What is the age of the child (or children) you're looking to claim Child Benefit for? Please let me know if you have:
- Children under 16 years old
- Children aged 16-19 years old
- Children aged 20 or over

If you have multiple children of different ages, please tell me about all of them, including their names and ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I've got one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and still living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son, **Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to determine Alex's current situation. For 16-19 year olds to qualify for Child Benefit, they typically need to be in education, training, or have recently left education and be eligible for an extension.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Is Alex currently in education or training?** This could be:
   - Full-time education (school, college, university)
   - An apprenticeship
   - Other approved training

2. **Or has he recently left education?** (within the last 20 weeks)

Please let me know which of these applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is currently in full-time education studying for his A-levels at sixth form college. That's great to know.

Let me navigate to the next check to verify the education level requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to verify that Alex's A-level education meets the specific requirements for Child Benefit.

**According to the rules for 16-19 year olds in education, the education must be:**
- **Non-advanced** (A-levels qualify - advanced education like university degrees do not)
- **Full-time** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

A-levels are approved education, so this looks promising! Let me ask a couple more clarifying questions:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time?** (i.e., is he undertaking at least 12 hours per week of supervised study at his sixth form college?)

2. **Is Alex married?** (This affects eligibility for 16-19 year olds - married 16-19 year olds only qualify if they're financially dependent on you)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing full-time A-levels - he's at college most days during the week. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is doing full-time A-levels at college, which clearly meets the supervised study requirement, and he's not married. This is good news.

Let me continue through the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if Alex is working. The rule is that 16+ year olds in approved education can work, but only up to a certain limit.

**Does Alex work?** 

- Is he in paid work? If yes, how many hours per week does he work?
- Or is he not working at all?

(The key threshold is that he needs to be working less than 24 hours per week to remain eligible while in approved education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not working at all, which means he easily meets this requirement.

Let me continue to the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving certain state benefits in his own right.

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in his own name)

Or is he **not receiving** these types of benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a student living at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is not receiving any state benefits in his own name. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's apprenticeship status (if any). Since Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form college, this should be straightforward, but let me confirm:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

- No, he's just in full-time A-level education at sixth form college (as you mentioned earlier)
- Or is he in some form of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just doing his A-levels at college like I said.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship - he's simply studying full-time A-levels at college.

Let me move forward to the next check, which is about your residency.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. For Child Benefit, the claimant (you) must meet UK residency requirements. There are several ways to qualify:

**The main paths are:**
1. **Normally live in the UK** - this is the most common route
2. **Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. Other special circumstances (pre-settled status with certain conditions, Crown servants abroad, etc.)

**Can you tell me - do you normally live in the UK?** 

Or if you have a different immigration status (such as pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme), please let me know and I can check if you meet the specific requirements for that route.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You normally live in the UK in Manchester. That satisfies the residency requirement.

Let me move to the next check about your responsibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check that you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** - you mentioned he's living at home with you
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** - you pay for food, clothes, housing, etc.
3. **You're paying maintenance** - under a court order or agreement

**Since you mentioned Alex is living at home with you, I assume you're responsible for him - is that correct?** You provide his food, housing, and other support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me and I provide for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You live with Alex and provide for him, so you're clearly responsible for him. That's another requirement satisfied.

Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent (if you're separated/divorced)
- Another guardian or relative
- Or is no one else claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is living and if any special circumstances apply.

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital
- In local authority care
- Fostered
- Or living normally at home with you (which is what you mentioned earlier)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just living normally at home with me - nothing special like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me proceed to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're nearly at the end. The final check is about whether the local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Or are you fully supporting him yourself without any council payments?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful! You're fully supporting Alex yourself without any council contributions. That means you've passed all the eligibility checks!

Let me provide you with your final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Congratulations! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to receive Child Benefit for your son Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Your Child:**
- **Alex** (age 18) ✓ Qualifies
  - In approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
  - Not working full-time
  - Not receiving disqualifying benefits
  - Living at home with you

**Your Situation:**
- ✓ Live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ Responsible for Alex (living with you and providing support)
- ✓ Sole claimant (no one else claiming for Alex)
- ✓ Local council not contributing to his support

### What You Need to Do Next:

To claim Child Benefit, you should:

1. **Apply online** at gov.uk or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year

### Important Note:

Child Benefit is payable **every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits). The payment will continue while Alex remains in approved education.

For more information or to claim online, visit: **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
